data.title: Close of pleadings
sentences: (1) This rule applies to pleadings between the following:
(a) a plaintiff and a defendant
(b) a plaintiff-by-counterclaim and a defendant-by-counterclaim
(c) a third party plaintiff and a third party defendant
(d) a plaintiff and a third party defendant.
(2) Pleadings close when
(a) a reply is filed and served by a plaintiff, plaintiff-by-counterclaim or third party plaintiff, as the case may be, or
(b) the time for filing and serving a reply expires, whichever is earlier.

(3) The close of pleadings against one party represents the close of pleadings against all parties to that pleading. *[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.67 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010]*
info_notes:
The time for filing and service of a reply is covered in earlier rules in this Part.
For example, rule 3.33 requires the plaintiff’s reply to be [Reply to a defence] filed and served on the defendant within  Hislop v. Murray, [2012] AWLD 4638, 219 ACWS (3d) 248 at para. 22 (Alta. Q.B. (Master)). days after service of the statement of defence on the plaintiff. See also rule 3.54(2) [Plaintiff’s reply to third party defence].

commentary.text: Close of pleadings is very important. It is the point when all of the issues in the action are framed. It is the starting point for the need for leave of the court or consent of all parties to amend pleadings pursuant to rule 3.62. Pleadings close when any one of the enumerated parties serves a reply, or the time for filing and serving a reply ( Hislop v. Murray, [2012] AWLD 4638, 219 ACWS (3d) 248 at para. 22 (Alta. Q.B. (Master)). days from receipt of the statement of defence) expires, whichever is earlier. Importantly, the close of pleadings against one party is the close of pleadings against all parties to that particular pleading.

data.title: Court options to deal with significant deficiencies
sentences: (1) If the circum- stances warrant and a condition under subrule
(2) applies, the Court may order one or more of the following:
(a) that all or any part of a claim or defence be struck out
(b) that a commencement document or pleading be amended or set aside
(c) that judgment or an order be entered
(d) that an action, an application or a proceeding be stayed.
(2) The conditions for the order are one or more of the following:
(a) the Court has no jurisdiction
(b) a commencement document or pleading discloses no reasonable claim or defence to a claim
(c) a commencement document or pleading is frivolous, irrelevant or improper
(d) a commencement document or pleading constitutes an abuse of process
(e) an irregularity in a commencement document or pleading is so prejudicial to the claim that it is sufficient to defeat the claim.
(3) No evidence may be submitted on an application made on the basis of the condition set out in subrule (2)(b).
(4) The Court may
(a) strike out all or part of an affidavit that contains frivolous, irrelevant or improper information
(b) strike out all or any pleadings if a party without sufficient cause does not
(i) serve an affidavit of records in accordance with rule 5.5 [When an affidavit of records must be served]
(ii) comply with rule 5.10 , or [Subsequent disclosure of records]
(iii) comply with an order under rule 5.11 [Order for a record to be produced]. *[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.68 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

data.title: Adding, removing or substituting parties to originating application
data.text:
(1) In an action started by originating application no party or person may be added or substituted as a party to the action except in accordance with this rule.
(2) On application of a party or person, the Court may order that a person be added or substituted as a party to the action, (a) in the case of a person to be added or substituted as an originating applicant, if consent of the person proposed to be added or substituted is filed with the application;
(b) in the case of an application to add or substitute a person as a respondent, or to remove or correct the name of a party, if the Court is satisfied the order should be made.
(3) The Court may not make an order under this rule if prejudice would result for a party that could not be remedied by a costs award, an adjournment or the imposition of terms.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.75 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

commentary.text:
Case law has imported the test from Former Rule 38(3), meaning that the applicant is required to show that the order sought would directly affect the intervenor in the enjoyment of its legal rights, and the question to be settled could not be effectually and completely settled unless the intervenor was a party. This second case involves a two-part test:
(a) whether the applicant has a legal interest in the outcome of the proceedings, which can be a direct financial or legal interest; and (b) whether it is “just and convenient” to add the person, or whether the interest of the person would not be adequately protected if it is not added to the proceeding. Alberta (Ethics Commissioner) Q.B.) starting at para. 9.

data.title: Action to be taken when defendant or respondent added
data.text:
(1) If a defendant or respondent is added to or substituted in an action, the plaintiff, originating applicant, plaintiff-by-counterclaim or third party plaintiff must, unless the Court otherwise orders, (a) amend the commencement document, as required, to name the new party, and (b) serve the amended commencement document on each of the other parties.
(2) Unless the Court otherwise orders, (a) in the case of a new defendant, the new defendant has the same time period to serve a statement of defence as the defendant had under rule 3.31 , and [Statement of defence]
(b) the action against the new defendant or new respondent, as the case may be, starts on the date on which the new party is added to or substituted in the action.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.76 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

data.title: Subsequent encumbrancers not parties in foreclosure action
data.text:
A plaintiff in a foreclosure action must not make any subsequent encumbrancer a party to the claim unless possession is claimed from the subsequent encumbrancer.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.77 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

data.title: Responsibility of parties to manage litigation
data.text:
The parties are respon- sible for managing their dispute and for planning its resolution in a timely and cost-effective way.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 4.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*
sentences: The parties are respon- sible for managing their dispute and for planning its resolution in a timely and cost-effective way. *[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 4.1 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

data.title: What the responsibility includes
data.text:
The responsibility of the parties to manage their dispute and to plan its resolution requires the parties:
(a) to act in a manner that furthers the purpose and intention of these rules described in rule 1.2 , [Purpose and intention of these rules]
(b) in an action categorized as a standard case, to respond in a substantive way and within a reasonable time to any proposal for the conduct of an action, (c) in an action categorized as a complex case, to meet or to adjust dates in a timely way in a complex case litigation plan, (d) when the complexity or the nature of an action requires it, to apply to the Court for direction, or request case management under rule 4.12 , and [Request for case management]
(e) to consider and engage in one or more dispute resolution processes described in rule 4.16(1) unless the [Dispute resolution processes]
Court waives that requirement.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 4.2 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

info_notes:
This Part does not apply to an action brought by originating application unless the parties otherwise agree or the Court otherwise orders. See rule 3.10 [Application of statement of and rule 3.12 claim rules to originating applications].
Under rule 8.4 [Trial date: scheduled by court clerk] no trial date can be scheduled by the court clerk until the parties have engaged in a dispute 4.16(2) can also be given in the course of an application under rule 8.5(1) [Trial date: scheduled by the judge]; see rule 8.5(1)(a)(iii).

commentary.text:
Rule 4.2 sets out the specific obligations of the parties under rule 4.1.
Rule 4.1 is a continuation of the expression of the foundational rules and it informs the responsibility of the parties set out in rule 4.1. This rule and the parties’ overriding responsibility is to act in accordance with rule 1.2 — fairly and justly resolving claims in a timely and cost-effective way.

data.title: Standard case obligations
sentences: (1) Unless the parties otherwise agree, or the Court otherwise orders, and subject to matters arising beyond the control of the parties, the parties to an action categorized as a standard case must, within a reasonable time considering the nature of the action, complete each of the following steps or stages in the action:
(a) close of pleadings

(b) disclosure of information under Part Ursa Ventures Ltd. v. Edmonton (City), [2016] A.J. No. 471, 2016 ABCA 135 at para. 96 (Alta. C.A.), Wakeling J.A. in dissent, although not expressly on this point.
[Disclosure of Information]
(c) at least one of the dispute resolution processes described in rule 4.16(1), unless the requirement is waived by the Court
(d) application for a trial date.

data.title: Settling disputes about complex case litigation plans
data.text:
If no agreement is reached on a complex case litigation plan within the period referred to in rule 4.5(1) , or if the parties cannot agree on an [Complex case obligations] adjustment to a date in the plan, the Court may (a) establish or amend a complex case litigation plan for the action, or (b) make a procedural order with respect to the action generally or to deal with particular issues or issues that may arise.

*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 4.6 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*
